synopsis: ASAM publishes OpenX scene and scenario formats, which help support a mature scenario-based structure for road vehicles, including scenario abstractions, catalogs and parameterised generation [f13223, f7410]. ASAM describes OpenX as in maintenance mode in 2026; the assessment anticipates slower core-format evolution and considers off-road extensions unlikely before mid-2027, though that timing remains uncertain [f7170, f13211, f7172]. ASAM's off-road workshop identified missing concepts for deformable and particle terrain, vegetation, heavy-machine manipulation and sensor degradation [f13213]. These gaps do not make OpenX unusable, but off-road work will require extensions or a manufacturer-owned domain model [f7196, f7434]. OpenX-linked components are assessed as requiring medium relative integration effort: existing transport and schemas help, but material, actor, dynamics and timing semantics still need calibration [f8729].

relations.note: Both report ASAM's maintenance-mode description for OpenX in 2026.
Both require off-road extensions or a manufacturer domain model without declaring OpenX unusable.
Maintenance status supports the forecast of slower evolution and delayed off-road extensions.
Missing off-road concepts explain the need for extensions or a manufacturer-owned domain model.
Workshop gaps substantiate the proposed off-road adaptation requirement.
Missing terrain and machine concepts help explain calibration effort despite standard schemas.
Mature road scenario specifications support the availability of standard schemas for integration.
Off-road concept gaps qualify the scope of the reported on-road maturity.
